title_en: Inner Mongolia Jiujun Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Yunzhou Commercial Building Co., Ltd. v. Han Fengbin, Shanghai Radio and Television Station, and Dalian Hongyan Pharmacy Co., Ltd. — retrial of jurisdiction objection in a dispute over product quality damage compensation
ruling_gist_en: For cases remanded for retrial by a higher people's court, whether the parties may raise an objection to jurisdiction again is not explicitly provided for in the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. full_text_en:
Inner Mongolia Jiujun Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.,  
Shanghai Yunzhou Commercial Building Co., Ltd. v. Han Fengbin,  
Shanghai Media Group, Dalian Hongyan Pharmacy Co., Ltd.  
— dispute over compensation for product quality damage (application for retrial of jurisdictional objection)

Ruling Summary

With respect to a case remanded for retrial by a higher people's court, whether the parties may raise a jurisdictional objection again is not explicitly provided for in the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. However, in accordance with the principle of jurisdictional finality, once the jurisdiction of a case remanded for retrial has been determined, if a party still raises a jurisdictional objection, the people's court shall not support it.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2013) Min Zai Shen Zi No. 27

Retrial Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Inner Mongolia Jiujun Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Domicile: Tuanjie Road, Longxingchang Town, Wuyuan County, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Li Lanji, Executive Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wan Jianxiong, Lawyer of Jiangxi Huabang Law Firm.

Retrial Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shanghai Yunzhou Commercial Building Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 88 Damuqiao Road, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Sun Zhiwei, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Hongyuan, Employee of the Company.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Han Fengbin, male, born on November 29, 1969, Han ethnicity, domiciled at Room 1-2-2, Building 12, Jinhuazhongyuan, Jinxiu Xiaoqu, Shahekou District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.

Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance: Shanghai Media Group. Domicile: No. 651 West Nanjing Road, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Li Ruigang, Director of the Group.

Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance: Dalian Hongyan Pharmacy Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 271 Changjiang Road, Zhongshan District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Gu Yusheng, Chairman of the Company.

The retrial applicants, Inner Mongolia Jiujun Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiujun Pharmaceutical) and Shanghai Yunzhou Commercial Building Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yunzhou Commercial Building), filed an application for retrial with this Court against the respondent Han Fengbin, and the defendants at first instance, Shanghai Media Group (hereinafter referred to as the Media Group) and Dalian Hongyan Pharmacy Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongyan Pharmacy), in relation to the civil ruling (2012) Liao Li Yi Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 1 rendered by the Liaoning High People's Court concerning a jurisdictional objection in a dispute over compensation for product quality damage. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review the matter, and the review is now concluded.

In the case of Han Fengbin v. Jiujun Pharmaceutical, Yunzhou Commercial Building, the Media Group, and Hongyan Pharmacy concerning a dispute over compensation for product quality damage, the Dalian Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province rendered a civil judgment (2007) Da Min Quan Chu Zi No. 4 on September 3, 2008. Jiujun Pharmaceutical, Yunzhou Commercial Building, and the Media Group were dissatisfied and appealed to the Liaoning High People's Court. That court rendered a civil judgment (2008) Liao Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 400 on May 24, 2010. After the judgment became legally effective, Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building applied to this Court for retrial. This Court issued a civil ruling (2010) Min Shen Zi No. 1019 on December 22, 2010, to bring the case up for retrial, and on August 3, 2011, issued a civil ruling (2011) Min Ti Zi No. 117, setting aside the first and second instance civil judgments and remanding the case to the Dalian Intermediate People's Court for retrial. During the retrial, Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building raised a jurisdictional objection.

The Dalian Intermediate People's Court ruled that the court had jurisdiction over the case for the following reasons: 1. The court's retrial of this case was pursuant to an instruction from the Supreme People's Court. 2. The domicile of one of the defendants, Hongyan Pharmacy, is at No. 271 Changjiang Road, Zhongshan District, Dalian City. The jurisdictional objection raised by Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building was not established. The court ruled to reject the jurisdictional objection raised by Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building.

Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building were dissatisfied and appealed. The Liaoning High People's Court ruled that when Han Fengbin filed the lawsuit with the Dalian Intermediate People's Court, he had already named Hongyan Pharmacy as a defendant, and during the original trial, he had submitted relevant evidence of purchasing medicine from Hongyan Pharmacy, which was examined and cross-examined at trial. Hongyan Pharmacy was a proper defendant. Pursuant to Article 22 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Dalian Intermediate People's Court had lawful jurisdiction over the case. The grounds of appeal raised by Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building were not sustainable. The court ruled to dismiss the appeal and uphold the original ruling.

Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building respectively filed applications for retrial with this Court, alleging: According to Article 21, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "a civil action brought against a legal person or other organization shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the defendant is domiciled," and Article 28, which provides that "an action arising from a tort shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the tort was committed or where the defendant is domiciled," the domiciles of the two defendants at first instance, Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building, are in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region and Shanghai, respectively. Their production and sales activities did not occur in Dalian, nor did they commit any tortious acts within the administrative area of Dalian. The case should not be under the jurisdiction of a court within the administrative area of Dalian, Liaoning Province, but rather under the jurisdiction of the Bayannur Intermediate People's Court of Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region or the Shanghai No.1 Intermediate People's Court. Moreover, the sales invoice submitted by the respondent Han Fengbin during the original trial showed the customer's name was not Han Fengbin, and it could not prove that the sale was made by Hongyan Pharmacy. The second instance ruling erred in finding Hongyan Pharmacy to be a proper defendant.

This Court holds: Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building raised their jurisdictional objection only after the case was remanded to the first instance court for retrial by this Court through the trial supervision procedure. With respect to the time period for a party to raise a jurisdictional objection, the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China explicitly provides: "If a party objects to the jurisdiction, it shall be raised within the period for filing a defense." In the initial first instance of this case, the plaintiff Han Fengbin's complaint was served on Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building. During the defense period, they did not raise any jurisdictional objection, indicating that they had accepted the jurisdiction of the first instance court, and the jurisdiction had been determined. Moreover, the case has gone through first instance, second instance, and retrial proceedings, and the procedures already completed remain procedurally effective and irreversible. Although according to the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, a case remanded for retrial is a first instance case and should be tried under first instance procedures, a case remanded for retrial is not an initial case. In terms of jurisdiction, the commencement of civil proceedings begins with the plaintiff's filing of the lawsuit, the purpose of which is to obtain a final adjudication from the court to resolve the civil dispute between the parties. When the case is filed with the people's court, accepted by the court, and the complaint is served on the defendant, if the defendant does not raise a jurisdictional objection within the defense period, it indicates that the court with jurisdiction over the case has been determined. Thereafter, the court with jurisdiction over the case shall not be changed due to changes in the domicile or habitual residence of the parties or changes in administrative divisions. With the jurisdiction already determined, the parties are not entitled to raise a jurisdictional objection again. If the parties could still raise a jurisdictional objection during the retrial, it would undoubtedly place the already stable litigation process in an uncertain state, undermining the stability and order of the proceedings, delaying the litigation, not only being detrimental to the resolution of the dispute but also wasting judicial resources. Therefore, based on the principle of jurisdictional finality, the certainty of litigation procedures, and the requirements of fairness and efficiency, a party in a retrial case cannot be supported in raising a jurisdictional objection again. Accordingly, there is no legal basis for Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building to raise a jurisdictional objection in this case, and the original trial court's ruling to reject their jurisdictional objection was not erroneous.

In summary, the retrial applications of Jiujun Pharmaceutical and Yunzhou Commercial Building do not meet the circumstances set forth in Article 200, Item (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 204, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

The retrial applications of Inner Mongolia Jiujun Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Yunzhou Commercial Building Co., Ltd. are rejected.

Presiding Judge: Zhang Zhihong  
Acting Judge: Ning Sheng  
Acting Judge: Jia Yaqi
